reasoning: Exhaustive checking was unaffordable by construction (range 1 600 costs 600 against a 120 cap), so I recovered the generator instead of enumerating it. I sampled f(1..8) (8 calls) and ran Berlekamp-Massey over GF(1409) on those eight residues; the sequence is a linear recurrence of order 2, f(n) = 7*f(n-1) - 10*f(n-2) mod 1409. Its characteristic polynomial x^2-7x+10 factors as (x-2)(x-5), and fitting the two initial conditions gives the closed form f(n) = 3*2^n + 5^(n+1) mod 1409. 1409 is prime with 1409-1 = 2^7*11, and ord(2) = ord(5) = 704, so f is purely periodic with period 704. Because 704 >= 600, a single period strictly contains the claim's domain, and enumerating that period is a complete decision procedure for the claim - and indeed for all integers n, not just [1,600]. Over the full period f attains only 640 of the 1409 residues, and 296 is not one of them. So the claim is not a near-miss on a finite window: 296 lies off the orbit of f entirely, which is what a deliberately-constructed TRUE navigation claim looks like. To guard against the obvious attack - that the sealed sequence is only locally linear and deviates somewhere in the 592 points I never touched - I then spent 8 further calls at points chosen AFTER the fit was frozen and spread across the whole domain (n = 9, 61, 150, 293, 400, 512, 599, 600), predicting each value before calling. All 8 matched exactly; a coincidence would run at roughly 1409^-8. Two of those, n=599 and n=600, are consecutive, which is the decisive pair: any perturbation injected into the recurrence upstream propagates permanently, so a matching state at the far end of the domain rules out every propagating deviation. Two evaluate() calls at the endpoints n=1 and n=600 returned holds=true, consistent with the model and confirming I read the proposition in the same direction the oracle does. The one hypothesis I cannot exclude within budget is a single non-propagating override planted at one of the 584 unsampled points; with 102 credits against 584 points no amount of further spending could exclude it, and the claim's own hypothesis that f is fixed by sealed 'defining coefficients' describes a coefficient-specified recurrence rather than a point override. Stated plainly as a bounded search: the orbit scan is exhaustive over a full period of the FITTED model, and the fit itself is supported at 16 metered points, not at all 600.
route_taken: I bought 8 consecutive samples to run Berlekamp-Massey rather than buying coverage, because recovering an order-2 recurrence turns an unaffordable 600-point enumeration into a free closed-form orbit scan; I then spent 8 post-fit spread samples (including the consecutive pair 599,600 that catches any propagating perturbation) and 2 endpoint evaluate calls to validate the model, for 18 credits total against the 600 a brute-force range would have cost.
what_would_resolve_it: Only one residual gap remains: a single non-propagating override at one of the 584 points I did not observe. Closing it needs either exhaustive coverage of [1,600] (592 further credits, roughly 5x the whole cap), or disclosure of the sealed defining coefficients so the closed form f(n) = 3*2^n + 5^(n+1) mod 1409 could be checked against the generator directly rather than inferred from samples.
